trust_decision.summary: Whether SQL submitted to a read-only tool may run is decided only by a leading-keyword classifier over dialect-tokenized statements (execute-sql/custom tool handlers); the connectors then execute it on a writable connection with no engine-level read-only enforcement.

landing_point.why: The summary says read-only mode lets writes through; the READONLY_VIOLATION gate in the execute_sql handler (and the isReadOnlySQL classifier it calls) is the obvious first stop.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:451-564 (and postgres/index.ts:598-666, mysql/index.ts:606-662, mariadb/index.ts:593-662): Connector.executeSQL, the engine layer below the handler's classifier, plus the dialect tokenizer src/utils/sql-parser.ts:135-142

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The handler already rejects non-read-only SQL before calling the connector, and the docs call read-only mode 'a safety net ... not a security boundary' (docs/tools/execute-sql.mdx:129), so a solver can argue tightening the classifier is enough and the connectors (and SQL Server, which has no READ ONLY transaction) are out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: One source connection is shared by read-only and writable tools: a writable execute_sql/custom tool on the same source must still be able to INSERT after a read-only call (so connection-level read-only or a sticky query_only/READ ONLY session breaks it); SQLite introspection PRAGMAs (table_info(t), bare 'PRAGMA user_version') and MySQL '-- ' comments must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: mysql/mariadb '--' followed by non-whitespace (minus operators) vs '-- ' / control char / DEL 0x7F / EOL (comment) (fix.diff:700-711)

SQLite PRAGMA parenthesized setter 'name(v)' incl. schema-qualified 'schema.name(v)', with allow-list for table_info/index_info/index_list/foreign_key_list (fix.diff:646-654, 674-677)
function-based writes passing the classifier, e.g. SELECT setval(...) (fix.diff:387-413)
single-statement vs multi-statement batch (postgres BEGIN READ ONLY on both paths; sqlite re-assert per statement) (fix.diff:427, 473-485)
parameterized vs unparameterized execution (custom tools pass parameters) (fix.diff:393-395)
in-batch backstop toggle 'PRAGMA query_only = OFF; INSERT ...' (fix.diff:470-475)

O7_producer.where: Closest analogue is the dialect tokenizer src/utils/sql-parser.ts:135-142 that produces statement boundaries; the check does call it (src/tools/execute-sql.ts:27), so it is not an uncalled producer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SQL Server connector executeSQL ignores options.readonly entirely; classifier-passing writes such as SELECT NEXT VALUE FOR <sequence> (sequence advance, analogue of setval) reach the engine with no backstop.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: SQL Server has no START TRANSACTION READ ONLY equivalent and the advisory/fix only touch PG/MySQL/MariaDB/SQLite, so it looks like an unsupported combination.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different connector file (src/connectors/sqlserver) from landing point src/tools/execute-sql.ts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MySQL/MariaDB tokenizer does not treat '#' as a line comment, so a quote after '#' makes the classifier see one SELECT while the engine sees a stacked statement; DDL then escapes the READ ONLY transaction (fix itself notes DDL implicit-commits).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the '--' differential; '#' looks like a different comment style and the engine backstop seems to cover it (it does not for DDL).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the published tokenizer fix, different scanner rule

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MySQL/MariaDB string scanner ignores backslash escapes (\'), so the classifier's string boundary differs from the engine's and a stacked DDL statement can be hidden inside what the parser thinks is a literal.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Backslash escaping depends on sql_mode (NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES), so a solver can call it configuration-dependent; shared scanner is also used by other dialects.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, shared string scanner used by all dialects

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SQL Server tokenizer uses the non-nesting block-comment scanner although T-SQL nests /* */ comments; with no engine backstop on SQL Server, a stacked statement hidden after a nested comment is unprotected.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory is about MySQL '--' and SQLite PRAGMA; SQL Server tokenizer was not mentioned and Postgres already uses a nesting scanner, so it looks deliberate.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different dialect scanner; pairs with sqlserver connector route

O8b_injection_room.sibling: EXPLAIN translation returns early from executeSQL before any readonly backstop added below it, so a backstop placed after this branch is skipped for the EXPLAIN route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Early-return special-casing at the top of executeSQL already exists; a maintainer adding a backstop lower in the function would naturally miss it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Custom tool checks the whole statement with isReadOnlySQL without splitting into statements (execute_sql splits at src/tools/execute-sql.ts:26-29); a stacked statement in a readonly custom tool passes the classifier.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Custom statements are config-authored, so a maintainer could reasonably skip splitting; it is a real asymmetry at the pinned commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Connector's own read/write split uses substring includes('table_info') on the statement, a second, independent classifier that could disagree with allowed-keywords.ts.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Duplicate PRAGMA allow-lists in connector and classifier already drift; a sibling here is a natural maintenance slip.

O9_family: Incomplete deny-list / parser differential in read-only SQL enforcement (CWE-184, CWE-863), missing engine-level authorization backstop
